body.statement: For \(K=2\), each \(t\in\mathcal T\), and each reported \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), characterize necessary and sufficient restrictions under which, on the face where all component risks and at-risk denominators are positive, \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t(x)\) is constant over \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) and equals \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm{obs}}_t(b)\). When the restrictions fail, the certificate must cover the exhaustive partition: give a finite separating certificate if the comparison face is empty; if it is nonempty and \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t\) is nonconstant, construct two vectors on that face whose compatible full-law lifts yield different values; if it is nonempty and \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t\) is constant but that constant differs from \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm{obs}}_t(b)\), give one compatible-law lift on the face and its controlled-risk calculation as an observable-mismatch certificate.
body.justification: The adjacent point-identification result should enter the larger external-margin analysis through an exact collapse boundary, not through an asserted class inclusion.
body.gap: Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and Proposition on marginal \(CSE_k\) identification) identify the time-to-event challenge subtype effect from at-risk event hazards under time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, a covariate-invariant exposure ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality; they do not characterize the identified set after those last identification restrictions are replaced by external exposure margins and a common-history fiber.
body.consumer: Vaccine researchers can determine when the published point-identified challenge subtype effect is recovered and when external surveillance supports only a nondegenerate compatible-law set.
